problem: Whether to invest heavily in original programming.
title: Netflix commits to two seasons of House of Cards without a pilot
context: Netflix was mainly a licensor of other studios' content and had never produced a major original series.
decision_made: Commit to at least 26 episodes of House of Cards, reportedly about $100 million, with no pilot.
action_taken: Netflix's chief content officer used viewing data to justify the bet; the amount was a rumour that Netflix did not confirm.
observed_outcome: Netflix's content chief said the show became its most-watched programme; one outside estimate said the investment was earned back through new subscribers, but Netflix gave no hard numbers.
lessons: Viewing data can support a large creative bet, but figures about returns are often outside estimates.
limitations: The $100 million figure was reported, not confirmed. Netflix declined to release viewing numbers. The payback estimate came from a third party.

claims.claim_text: Netflix committed to a minimum of 26 episodes of House of Cards, reported at about $100 million.
Netflix's viewing data was said to have supported the bet.
An outside calculation estimated the investment was recouped through added subscribers.
